subject: How to decide a DIF item?

messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: How to decide a DIF item?
parts:
Hi Phil,

I was following the manuals of mirt to plot my DIF items, using p=0.01 cut-off point. And, for the couple DIF plots, I found that some effect sizes are small and some are big (visually). I wonder if you would recommend any readings (or you have any thought), regarding the final decision-making of a DIF item? I feel like using p=0.01 makes sense for the statistical-significance cut-off values, and I am more curious about the clinical significance. 

Thank-you in advance,
Yingyi

I am following the example codes in the DRF() documentation of the mirt package, using my own dataset. 

Using multipleGroup(), item3 is the DIF item.

Then I used the following codes: 
plot(mod1_scalar2)
plot(mod1_scalar2, which.items = 3) #DBF
plot(mod1_scalar2, type = 'itemscore')
plot(mod1_scalar2, type = 'itemscore', which.items = 3)
DRF(mod1_scalar2)
DRF(mod1_scalar2, focal_items = 3) #DBF
DRF(mod1_scalar2, DIF=TRUE)
DRF(mod1_scalar2, DIF=TRUE, focal_items = 3)
DRF(mod1_scalar2, plot = TRUE)

However, the last 2 lines of codes had some error message:

I wonder what is the problem here? 

Thanks in advance,

messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: Re: How to decide a DIF item?
parts:
Hi Phil,

Me and my PI's project is moving along, with the biggest help from this mirt package. Thank-you again, and as always! I have few more questions here, associated with all the decision-making of DIF items through this whole process. So I decided to post them all in this post, just in case anyone else has the same issue. Apologies for any naive question, as I have no background in psychometrics (but keep improving now!)

Say I have an item bank with 9 items, 5-point scale. And there is no testlet (bundle) in the item bank. One-dimension. 

1. When using the multipleGroup(), to what extent we should refer to the item information trace lines? When using the p=0.01, the multipleGroup() returns 3 DIF items, i.e. item4, item8, item9. However, from the plot I attached, I feel like maybe there are more DIF items than 3? For example, item2, item5 and item6. This confusing results also happened for my other item banks. 

2. After multipleGroup(), if I want to see if the identified 3 DIF items are significant at the test level (i.e. clinical significance), should I just proceed with DRF()? Basically what I used as the codes are:

mod <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group=group, SE=TRUE,
invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))
plot(mod)
plot(mod, which.items = 6:10) #DBF
plot(mod, type = 'itemscore')
plot(mod, type = 'itemscore', which.items = 10:15)
DRF(mod)
DRF(mod, focal_items = 6:10) #DBF
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE)
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, focal_items = 10:15)
DRF(mod, plot = TRUE)
DRF(mod, focal_items = 6:10, plot = TRUE) #DBF
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, plot = TRUE)
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, focal_items = 10:15, plot = TRUE)
mirtCluster()
DRF(mod, draws = 500)
DRF(mod, draws = 500, plot=TRUE)

My question is, what if I don't have any bundles? And since I have 3 DIF items, I wonder how should I test them. Together (3 at a time), or 1 at a a time, or 2 at a time? I kinda confused here, how do I know which DIF item(s) cause the significant sDRF/uDRF? 

3. If there is only one single DIF item identified from multipleGroup(), should I just refer to the final sDRF and uDRF (to see if NEITHER of them are significant?) Sorry, I am a bit confused here, in making decision as whether to say a DIF item is DIF, or not...

4. My last question is, do the steps described above the correct sequence of identifying DIF? And, do I need more steps, and if I miss anything? 


Thank-you as always!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to decide a DIF item?
parts:
On Fri, Nov 16, 2018 at 7:40 PM <yingyi....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

Me and my PI's project is moving along, with the biggest help from this mirt package. Thank-you again, and as always! I have few more questions here, associated with all the decision-making of DIF items through this whole process. So I decided to post them all in this post, just in case anyone else has the same issue. Apologies for any naive question, as I have no background in psychometrics (but keep improving now!)

Say I have an item bank with 9 items, 5-point scale. And there is no testlet (bundle) in the item bank. One-dimension. 

1. When using the multipleGroup(), to what extent we should refer to the item information trace lines? When using the p=0.01, the multipleGroup() returns 3 DIF items, i.e. item4, item8, item9. However, from the plot I attached, I feel like maybe there are more DIF items than 3? For example, item2, item5 and item6. This confusing results also happened for my other item banks.

You have to keep in mind sampling error affects these plots. So although you are seeing potentially large functional differences the parameter estimates are too variable, and can dramatically change in new samples. Hence, raw observations are not always reliable, which is why we have statistical tests.

2. After multipleGroup(), if I want to see if the identified 3 DIF items are significant at the test level (i.e. clinical significance), should I just proceed with DRF()? Basically what I used as the codes are:

mod <- multipleGroup(dat, model, group=group, SE=TRUE,
invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var'))
plot(mod)
plot(mod, which.items = 6:10) #DBF
plot(mod, type = 'itemscore')
plot(mod, type = 'itemscore', which.items = 10:15)
DRF(mod)
DRF(mod, focal_items = 6:10) #DBF
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE)
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, focal_items = 10:15)
DRF(mod, plot = TRUE)
DRF(mod, focal_items = 6:10, plot = TRUE) #DBF
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, plot = TRUE)
DRF(mod, DIF=TRUE, focal_items = 10:15, plot = TRUE)
mirtCluster()
DRF(mod, draws = 500)
DRF(mod, draws = 500, plot=TRUE)

My question is, what if I don't have any bundles? And since I have 3 DIF items, I wonder how should I test them. Together (3 at a time), or 1 at a a time, or 2 at a time? I kinda confused here, how do I know which DIF item(s) cause the significant sDRF/uDRF?
If you care only about DIF then focus on one item at a time. If you care about the bundle effects then do those.

3. If there is only one single DIF item identified from multipleGroup(), should I just refer to the final sDRF and uDRF (to see if NEITHER of them are significant?) Sorry, I am a bit confused here, in making decision as whether to say a DIF item is DIF, or not...

Sure, that seems reasonable. They represent measures of effect sizes, so it's analogous to reporting a Cohen's d-type estimate after a t-test is used in an independent samples means test, for example.
4. My last question is, do the steps described above the correct sequence of identifying DIF? And, do I need more steps, and if I miss anything?
Depends on your data and degree of complexity you're going for. I unfortunately can't answer that with any confidence.
Thank-you as always!
